display_name: Toy Story 2: Buzz Lightyear to the Rescue
subtitle: BizHawk
_subtitle_source: subtitle names the backend the player will actually run, the same way 18 manifests say "BizHawk".
_platform_source: the world's own setup guide: "A legally obtained copy of Toy Story 2: Buzz Lightyear to the Rescue (PS1, NTSC-U ...)" and "[BizHawk] 2.10 or later ... Under Config > Preferred Cores > PSX, select Nymashock."
_drafted_note: Drafted 2026-08-25 from the world's OWN repository -- its __init__.py, archipelago.json, setup guide and README, read that day. No field is filled in from memory or from what other games on the same console do.
_ap_world_name_source: READ FROM THE WORLD'S OWN CODE: Source Code/__init__.py line 156, `class ToyStory2World(World)` sets `game: ClassVar[str] = "Toy Story 2"`. ⚠ The ClassVar annotation is why a plain `game =` search finds nothing here -- the value is the World's all the same. NOT the full retail title: the display name carries the subtitle and the AP slot name does not.
description: Toy Story 2: Buzz Lightyear to the Rescue as a multiworld. Moves, gadgets, level unlocks and Pizza Planet tokens are shuffled across 15 levels. Requires the player's own NTSC-U disc, BizHawk 2.10 or newer with the Nymashock PSX core, and the world's own ts2.lua script loaded in BizHawk's Lua Console.
_description_source: written by us from the world's own structure and its setup guide's stated requirements. No text is copied from the game.
_checks_verified_note: FALSE. Nobody has played this. For a kind=world game the checks travel through the WORLD'S client, not through London -- so what is unproven here is not a RAM map of ours (there is none) but the whole chain: apworld installs, emulator starts over the bridge, the world's client attaches and carries a check. London warns at launch while this is false, which is exactly right until a tester reports one.
_requires_source: PSX title. The setup guide lists it among the player's own requirements: "A legally obtained copy of Toy Story 2 ... as an ISO or BIN/CUE image."

rom.description: Your own Toy Story 2: Buzz Lightyear to the Rescue disc image for PlayStation 1 -- the NTSC-U release, disc serial SLUS-00893. Other regions and REV releases are not supported
rom._description_source: the world's README, word for word: "(PS1, NTSC-U, serial `SLUS-00893`) as an ISO or BIN/CUE image. Other regions are not supported, and revision (REV) releases will not work." ⚠ THE WORLD CONTRADICTS ITSELF: its docs/setup_en.md gives the serial as `SCUS-94464` for the same release. The README's value is used here because it is the more detailed and more recently written of the two, and the disagreement is recorded rather than smoothed over. Nothing in London checks the serial, so this text is what the player reads, not something the launcher enforces.
rom._hash_note: No hash is claimed. Neither document states a checksum. ⚠ The README warns that this matters more than usual here: "The client cannot detect a wrong disc -- it will connect and then behave incorrectly."

emulator.name: BizHawk
emulator._source: the setup guide, word for word: "[BizHawk] 2.10 or later (the latest release is recommended). Other emulators are not supported." Stated as a floor, so recorded as a minimum.

client.name: Toy Story 2 Client
client._name_source: the world registers it under this exact name, and its setup guide tells the player to expect it: "You should now find 'Toy Story 2 Client' in the list on the right side."
client._kind_source: the world ships and registers its OWN Archipelago client: Source Code/__init__.py does `components.append(Component(...))` with `component_type=Type.CLIENT`, under a comment that says what it is -- "Register a 'Toy Story 2 Client' button in the Archipelago Launcher with the TS2 icon." The world also ships its OWN BizHawk connector, ts2.lua, as a release asset, which the guide has the player place in Archipelago/data/lua/ and load from BizHawk's Lua Console: "This single script does everything, so you do not need to load any separate Archipelago BizHawk connector." The Lua belongs to them, not to us -- the same shape as glover and tomba in this catalogue. London must NOT read memory for this game.
client._protocol_source: extensions/bizhawk/extension.json declares {"protocol": "bizhawk"} and BizHawkBridge.Systems includes "PSX". The world targets BizHawk explicitly and names the core: "Under Config > Preferred Cores > PSX, select Nymashock."
client._lua_note: No Lua of OURS. The world ships its own connector, ts2.lua, which the player loads in BizHawk's Lua Console -- so this field stays null rather than naming a script London does not provide.

apworld._source: the author's own releases page; the newest release read 25 Aug 2026 is 2.2.0, carrying toystory2.apworld and ts2.lua. ⚠ BOTH assets are needed -- the apworld alone will not send a check.
apworld._world_version_source: the newest release tag on imklubb/Archipelago-Toy-Story-2, read via the GitHub API 25 Aug 2026. The world carries no archipelago.json, so the tag is the only version it states.
apworld._minimum_ap_version_source: the setup guide: "Please use version 0.6.7 or later for integrated BizHawk support." Our client is 0.6.7, so this is exactly met.

_patch_extension_source: read from the world's own source, 25 Aug 2026: the 8 .py files in Source Code/ were searched. No APPatchExtension, no APProcedurePatch, no patch_file_ending -- this world produces no patch container. The guide agrees: the player boots their own unmodified disc and loads ts2.lua.
_patch_note: There is deliberately NO `patch` block: the world produces no patch container and the player's disc is never modified.

world_by.name: imklubb
world_by._authors_source: the GitHub account that publishes the world (the repository owner). The world carries no archipelago.json and no credits list, so this may name a maintainer rather than every author.
world_by._source: the repository the world is published from; its own source, archipelago.json and setup guide are what this manifest was written against.
world_by._licence_source: the repository has no LICENSE file -- the GitHub API reports license: null (25 Aug 2026). We redistribute none of this world's code; the player downloads it from the author's own release.

credits._game_by_note: Not recorded rather than guessed. The game is the property of its publisher and is never distributed here; the player supplies their own copy. The Archipelago world is its authors' work. Only the plugin itself is by solida1987.

_author_disclosure: The world's own README opens with: "Please note, this was created with the assistance of AI." Recorded because it is the author's own published statement about their world. It is not a judgement.
